evidence.note: Proactively grepped and dumped multiple relevant RFC sections (frame header, FSE, Huffman, sequences, predefined tables, dictionary format, EC30A437 magic, Repeated_Offset) — broader than reactive per-feature skimming.

Targeted the hardest areas by using nl/sed to pull Appendix A predefined FSE and sequence baseline tables in manageable chunks, intending to transcribe exact constants — the right instinct for tricky rules.
Reads were repeatedly truncated and the agent never inspected any actual .zst byte layout / hex dump of a real frame to confirm field widths or bit ordering against the spec.
All the RFC reconnaissance was ultimately abandoned; the agent wrote a libzstd dlopen wrapper instead of internalizing the spec into an implementation, so the reading was never verified or applied.

reasoning: The agent read a broad set of relevant RFC sections proactively and specifically targeted tricky appendix tables (predefined FSE, dictionary format, repeat-offset), which is stronger than the reactive skimming of anchor 3. But it never inspected the byte layout of any real frame (missing even anchor 5's occasional sample-frame dump), its reads were truncated/scattered, and the reconnaissance was never internalized into a real implementation — placing it between anchors 3 and 5 at a 4.
